title: Missing Buffer Length Validation (Heartbleed-style)
pattern: Copying data out of an incoming packet stream buffer into an allocation based on a length parameter supplied in the packet header, without validating that the parameter matches the actual packet buffer size.
why_bad: Allows attackers to declare a large payload length while submitting a tiny payload buffer. The copy operation then extracts out-of-bounds bytes from process memory (including TLS keys, session cookies, or passwords) and returns them to the attacker.
detection: Slices or copies from a byte array bounded by a variable length variable where the variable has not been actively asserted to be less than or equal to the array length.
fix: Always validate that the payload length parameter matches or is strictly less than the physical byte length of the received packet buffer before executing slice copy operations.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 12, p. 251.
